messages:
Evan (support): Heads-up — Acme reported being double-charged and seeing repeated 401 auth errors after bumping to `redwood-python==1.20.0`. They say it started immediately after pip upgrade. Repro steps they gave below. Anyone seen this? :grimacing:

Priya (eng): Can you paste the minimal repro and any client config? My hunch: we changed retry behavior and removed `timeout_ms` alias in 1.20 which could be causing a silent fallback + retry loop if auth refresh fails.

Evan (support): Repro from customer (sanitized):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"***\", timeout_ms=2000)  # was valid in 1.19
resp = client.generate(prompt=\"hello\")
print(resp)
```
Logs they attached: `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'timeout_ms'` then later client retries produce two near-identical requests (same body) and customer sees two billable tokens.

acme-support: Confirmed. We upgraded from 1.19 -> 1.20 and saw 2 requests per user action for a ~10 minute window. We added tracing and see identical payloads with two different request IDs.

Liam (infra): Do we have request IDs/trace ids for the pair? If they hit our gateway twice we can check whether one auth refresh triggered a reissue and a retry. Evan — can you ask for the x-request-id header values?

Evan (support): Sent request IDs to customer and they returned: `rwx-99a` and `rwx-99b` (same minute).

Priya (eng): Ok that matches a known pattern: if the SDK raises on invalid init kwarg, some code paths can create a client object partially and trigger an unauthenticated call + client-side retry. In 1.20 we renamed `timeout_ms` -> `timeout` and tightened signature (we should have thrown at import time, not partially construct).

Maya (billing): We see matching double-charge rows for those request IDs in the billing table. Amount small per event but customer upset. We should offer credit if confirmed and give pin instructions.

Priya (eng): Immediate mitigation for customers: pin to 1.19 with `pip install redwood-python==1.19.*` OR set an idempotency header on the calling side while we patch. Quick example: add `Idempotency-Key` header so repeated requests are deduplicated server-side:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import uuid
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"***\")
headers = {\"Idempotency-Key\": str(uuid.uuid4())}
resp = client.generate(prompt=\"hello\", extra_headers=headers)
```
Note: `extra_headers` is supported in 1.19; in some 1.20 installs it may fail — so pin first if you see the init error.

Priya (eng): Engineering action plan: (1) reproduce locally with 1.20 and the `timeout_ms` arg, (2) add a defensive check in client init to fail fast on unknown kwargs, (3) hotfix release 1.20.1 that restores compatibility alias or raises a clear error, (4) coordinate credits with billing.

Liam (infra): I'll correlate gateway traces for the two request ids and confirm whether both requests hit the model pool (or if second was a retry after auth refresh).

Evan (support): I provided the workaround and pin instructions to the customer and set expectation for credits if we confirm duplicate billing. They asked for a repro script we can run in-house — attaching sanitized sample and permission to run.

Priya (eng): Thx. Quick local repro I used to validate: create a venv, `pip install redwood-python==1.20.0`, run the snippet with `timeout_ms` kwarg — you should see the TypeError then multiple outgoing requests. I can open a draft PR for 1.20.1 after we confirm root cause.

deploy-bot: Noted: rollout that introduced signature change was tagged `client/1.20/strict-signature` and deployed 2026-03-12 21:04 UTC.

Maya (billing): I'll prepare a provisional one-off credit for Acme once eng confirms duplicate billing window and request count.

Priya (eng): Action items: @Liam check traces, @Evan confirm repro run, I will draft fix and a short release note recommending pinning if you can't patch immediately. Also add a snippet to migration docs showing `timeout` alias and `Idempotency-Key` guidance.

Evan (support): Thanks — I told Acme we'll follow up within 24 hrs with either a patch ETA or credit confirmation. :thumbsup:
